workflows.title: Scan intake: classify receipts/contracts into expense tracker.csv
workflows.trigger: A new scanned document file appears in the local Paperwork/Inbox folder (scanner/printer output).
workflows.outcome: tracker.csv gains a new row with normalized filename, date, amount, type and a status; the scanned file is renamed on disk to match; exceptions (duplicate vendor+date+amount match, amount over 500, missing/unreadable date) are flagged with a note instead of silently filed.
variations: Normal case: date/amount/type all legible -> status 'filed'.
Duplicate case (scan-0417): same vendor/date/amount already filed -> status 'duplicate', original file not renamed, note cites the matching prior filename.
High-value case (scan-0418, 780.00 EUR Studio Equipment): amount over 500 -> status 'review needed', note 'over 500'; no further action on this item found in captured evidence.
Missing-date case (scan-0415): date unreadable -> new_filename uses 'UNKNOWN-DATE' prefix, status still 'filed', note 'missing date'.
Type sometimes inferred from an external client list rather than the document itself (scan-0420 note: 'type from client list').
Naming convention change (2026-10-18): new_filename pattern changed from DATE_NAME_TYPE.pdf to TYPE_DATE_NAME.pdf per naming-rule-update.txt ('From today, filed receipts are named:
limitations: Only UI/accessibility text from Preview, TextEdit and Finder was inspected; no direct filesystem metadata was queried.
No resolution was found for the single 'review needed' flagged item.
No ordered capture example covers every step end-to-end.
The naming-convention change was observed once on 2026-10-18; no evidence of periodic recurrence of such rule changes.
No ordered capture example covers every step. These references do not establish one end-to-end occurrence.

workflows.title: File incoming project PDFs from email into project folders and confirm by reply
workflows.trigger: An email arrives from a known Northbeam colleague (e.g. Alex Moreau, Priya Shah) with a project PDF attachment and a request to save/file it.
workflows.outcome: The PDF is exported via Save As into the named project folder (Atlas or Beacon) and the sender receives a short reply confirming it was filed.
variations: Atlas project brief (10-14): saved as Atlas-project-brief.pdf, reply 'Hi Alex, got it, saved with the Atlas files. Thanks, Morgan'.
Beacon budget v2 (10-16): saved as Beacon-budget-v2.pdf, reply 'Thanks Priya, filed in the Beacon folder. Morgan'.
Atlas timeline (10-17): saved as Atlas-timeline.pdf; Morgan also opened the saved PDF in Preview (12:22:50) before replying 'Saved next to the brief. Thanks Alex' (12:24:14-26).
limitations: Only 3 instances were found within the available capture window (2026-10-14 to 2026-10-17); cadence beyond this week is unknown.
The Preview step on 10-17 shows the PDF's own content, not any save-confirmation UI; reported as an observed action rather than a verified verification step.
No single ordered capture example covers every step for the 10-14 and 10-16 runs; the 10-17 run has the most complete sequence including a Finder listing of the destination folder.
No ordered capture example covers every step. These references do not establish one end-to-end occurrence.
